elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) retains "Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause" — the frequency figure is redacted and unchanged in the rendered text, so no once-per-12-month cap is established; the "unless for cause" carve-out also leaves the cap open-ended.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) still reads "at least [***] prior notice"; the notice period remains an undefined redacted figure and is not expressly stated to be written.
No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in Section 9.9 as rendered.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a): "permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, to audit the books and records".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: 9.9(d): the Parties "shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence"; 9.9(b) also bars disclosure of the audited Party's Confidential Information beyond verification needs.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: Section 9.9 contains no off-site/remote-review preference; it simply requires the audited Party to permit the auditor to audit books and records maintained under Section 9.8.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: 9.9(c) allocates full cost to the auditing Party unless underpayment "was more than [***] percent" — the threshold is redacted and unchanged, so the 5% trigger is not established (undefined trigger).

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) limits the exercise to an independent third-party auditor reviewing "the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8" for payment-verification purposes only; no clause grants Vendor (or the auditor) access to Customer systems or remote access.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The claimed edit (operation index 2) does not exist in the rendered language; 9.9(a) still says "not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause". Deterministic check "audit frequency limited" = false and element coverage gate reports "Element references invalid operation 2".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: No inserted figure in the rendered text; 9.9(a) still reads "at least [***] prior notice". Coverage gate: "Element references invalid operation 1".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: 9.9(c) as rendered still says "more than [***] percent"; no 10% figure was inserted. Coverage gate: "Element references invalid operation 3".

reasons: The redline is not position-complete at either level: the rendered operative language is identical to the original. All three claimed fallback insertions are phantom — the element mapping points to operation indexes 1, 2 and 3 that do not exist, and the deterministic coverage gate flags each as "Element references invalid operation".

Frequency: replace "[***] in a given Calendar Year" in 9.9(a) with an express "once in any Calendar Year" (preferred: "once in any 12-month period"). Consider also narrowing or qualifying the open-ended "unless for cause" carve-out, which otherwise leaves the annual cap without a hard ceiling.

Notice: replace "at least [***] prior notice" in 9.9(a) with "at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" (preferred: thirty (30) days' written notice). A redacted figure is an undefined trigger and cannot satisfy the checklist.

Cost shifting: replace "more than [***] percent" in 9.9(c) with "more than ten percent (10%)" (preferred: five percent (5%)). Until a number is inserted, the cost-allocation element depends on an undefined trigger.

Preferred-only gaps (not required if the fallback is completed): no business-hours limitation and no "off-site where possible" language in Section 9.9. The independent-auditor, auditor-confidentiality and no-systems-access elements are already satisfied by 9.9(a), (b) and (d) and should be retained untouched.

Minimality and intent are not offended — nothing was added, deleted or paraphrased — but that is because no operative change was actually rendered. The rationale's proposed mutual insertion of the three figures would be minimal if it is actually executed as three targeted numeric substitutions in 9.9(a) and 9.9(c) with no other edits.
